palette.notes: No clips for this subject; the reference does not discuss colour. Palette is whatever the still scene uses.

lighting: Not covered by the reference; the frozen scene carries the lighting, and moving parts (signs, rain, smoke) are usually where light changes.
silhouette: The still scene is the composition; the one moving element must sit in a clear spot so the eye finds it.

motion.timing: One small, contained motion loops forever while everything else stays frozen; the end frame joins the first with no visible jump.

texture: Not covered by the reference beyond the still image itself.
camera: Locked: the camera never moves, otherwise the frozen area would read as a mistake.

acting.enters: No characters in the reference; a person may be in the frame but frozen.
acting.acts: One small action repeats (hair blowing, water rippling, a blink) while the rest holds still.
acting.depth: Not covered; staging lesson is that one moving part draws the eye wherever it sits.

techniques: freeze the whole scene, animate one small element
seamless loop: last frame flows into the first
use the still/moving contrast to point the eye
locked camera so the frozen part reads as intentional
feel: frozen scene + one looping detail = calm, hypnotic, the eye goes straight to what moves
for_fred: Between gags, hold the whole reel still and let only one thing loop (Pixie's tail flick, Fred's fin, a blinking cursor) so the next big move reads as an event. Avoid animating everything at once; that is the overuse Robert complained about.
